items.item: Moves presentation (swing animation/sound) to the client immediately on input
Server still validates hits (cooldown, range, timing) and applies damage
Adds impact feedback channels: hitstop, impact sound, VFX, camera shake, target reaction
Puts latency in anticipation/wind-up rather than the impact; or mentions Server Authority prediction as an option
Uses animation markers or timing to sync hit frames

slop: Haptics row and the ContextActionService/touch/gamepad aside don't address the question
'Apex:' header and the no-memory/no-Studio-connection preamble add nothing
overengineering: NaN/inf validation of a swingId the server never uses

incorrect_or_stale: The server code uses an undefined hitPosition
HitEffect:FireAllClients also fires to the attacker, who already played the effect locally, so they see it twice
slop: Input buffering, combos and lunge are genre-default mechanics the question didn't ask for
Generic hardening advice (rate-limit all remotes, network ownership, flag suspicious patterns)
overengineering: The rewind snapshot system is laid out in detail, but it's optional for melee

raw.reason: A meets every rubric item: it handles misprediction cleanly, puts latency into the wind-up, mentions Server Authority, and avoids double effects; B leaves out the anticipation idea and its sample code has a double-effect bug and an undefined variable.
